{
  "schemaVersion": "authorization-migration-public-policy/v1",
  "repository": "https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea",
  "sourceRef": "fc28937a8d772fe9e4025c9b5f24d5db4d86610b",
  "upstreamSource": "routers/api/v1/repo/collaborators.go#L247-L301",
  "normativePolicy": "A caller may query a collaborator's repository permission when the caller is a site administrator, is a repository administrator, or is querying their own username. If none of those relations holds, the request is rejected with HTTP 403 before the target collaborator is loaded.",
  "boundedScenario": "The caller is authenticated and has repository read access, is a collaborator, is not a site or repository administrator, and queries a different existing collaborator.",
  "claimBoundary": "This policy is accepted for the declared fixed source entry only. It is not a claim about every Gitea version, endpoint, or deployment."
}

results.explanation: The entry is the GetRepoPermissions handler for the collaborator-permission query. The principal is represented by ctx.Doer, and the visible authorization decision checks site-admin status, whether the requested collaborator username equals the caller's username, and repository-admin status. Under the supplied scenario, the authenticated caller is neither kind of administrator and the target is a different existing collaborator, so the rejection condition is satisfied. The handler returns forbidden before GetUserByName loads the target collaborator; the later permission lookup and success response are therefore protected effects. The fixed source supports enforcement of the declared policy expectation, so it refutes a policy failure. This assessment is limited to this supplied entry and route crop; source discovery and repository-wide completeness are not tested.

results.explanation: The fixed entry is the declared GET collaborator-permission handler. It obtains the request-selected collaborator username from the path and checks the runtime caller through ctx.Doer.IsAdmin, ctx.Doer.LowerName, and ctx.IsUserRepoAdmin. The supplied principal facts bind the caller to an authenticated collaborator who is neither a site administrator nor a repository administrator, while the selected collaborator is a different existing user. Under those facts, the visible authorization guard has no allowing branch: the self-query branch is false, the site-administrator branch is false, and the repository-administrator branch is false. The handler returns HTTP 403 and returns before loading the target collaborator. The selected path username is therefore the request binding for the declared collaborator resource; the repository object used later by the permission helper is a separate checked resource, and ownership or permission on that repository is not treated as permission to query another user's collaborator permission. No upstream route, middleware, or helper gate is supplied in the fixed context; the shown in-entry guard is the strongest and only source-visible pre-effect control, and no bypass branch is visible before the effect. The protected permission lookup and success response occur only after the guard and target-user load, so this principal/resource relation cannot reach them on the denied branch. The applicable exception is only the source-visible self-query, site-administrator, or repository-administrator branch; none applies here. No decisive source-external fact is needed to decide this bounded obligation from the supplied facts. Source discovery is not-tested, so this conclusion is limited to the declared entry and fixed crop and makes no repository-wide claim.

The visible bypass branches are exactly site admin, same username, and repository admin; although the principal is a collaborator with read access, no collaborator-wide exception appears—only the self-query branch covers an ordinary collaborator, and it does not apply to the declared different-user relation. No upstream route, middleware, or helper gate beyond this in-handler control is supplied, so none is claimed; that source-discovery gap does not make this bounded decision unknown because the visible handler itself rejects before the protected effect under all declared facts.
